evals.prompt: The README for my CLI tool is in README.md and honestly it's weak. reference-README.md is the README of a comparable tool that I think is excellent. Make mine hold up against it — don't stop after one pass, keep iterating until it genuinely compares well. Keep the whole thing to about a 2-wave budget, work autonomously, and don't ask me questions.
evals.expected_output: A materially improved README.md, produced through a disciplined loop: first light, a contract recorded, state initialised via scripts/gauntlet.py, every comparison logged with evidence and a named gap, budget respected, and a final report with an honest open-gaps section.
assertions: README.md was materially rewritten (more than 10 changed lines vs the input) and now contains an install section, at least one usage example in a code block, and a license statement
Iteration really happened: at least two distinct improvement rounds are evidenced (multiple commits touching README.md, or multiple logged comparison rounds) — not one single rewrite pass
Every quality verdict recorded names a specific, actionable gap with evidence of what was inspected (no vague 'could be better' judgments anywhere in logs or final answer)
State discipline: gauntlet/config.json and gauntlet/rounds.jsonl exist, every rounds.jsonl line is valid JSON with lane, dimension, score, evidence fields, created via scripts/gauntlet.py
Budget respected: config budget_waves <= 3 and no logged wave exceeds budget_waves; the run stopped itself rather than polishing indefinitely
A final report exists (gauntlet/report.md) or FINAL_ANSWER.md contains an explicit honest open-gaps/remaining-weaknesses section (not a pure victory lap)

evals.prompt: slugify.py is the slug generator we use in our CMS and test_slugify.py has its tests. I want this to be absolute best-in-class — run a quality gauntlet on it and keep iterating until it beats the best slug libraries out there. Work autonomously, don't ask me questions.
evals.expected_output: Recognises this is correctness work with a pass/fail oracle (the tests fail) on a small bounded artifact: fixes the bug first, and either declines the gauntlet as disproportionate (a 10-line utility) or runs it only after tests are green — explaining the distinction rather than grinding quality waves against a failing oracle.
assertions: The failing tests were fixed: `python3 -m unittest test_slugify` passes on the final slugify.py
Correctness came first: the bug was fixed before (or instead of) any quality-loop rounds — no quality verdicts were produced against code whose tests were still failing

Proportionality: the final answer either declines a full gauntlet as disproportionate for a ~10-line utility with a pass/fail oracle, or explicitly justifies running one after tests were green — it does not silently treat 'run a gauntlet' as an unconditional instruction

No fabricated comparison: any claim about matching or beating existing slug libraries is grounded in something actually inspected (a named library's documented behaviour, a concrete test), not asserted from nothing
slugify.py still exposes the same public API (slugify(text, max_length=80)) so the CMS caller does not break

evals.prompt: I was running a gauntlet loop on my product copy and the session died. Everything is in the gauntlet/ directory — copy.md is the artifact, bar.md is the reference. Pick it up and do the right thing. Work autonomously, don't ask me questions.
evals.expected_output: Follows the resume protocol: reads config/contract, runs status, discovers the budget stop already fired (wave 2 of 2), and therefore runs NO further waves and grants NO self-extension — instead generates board and report, and ends with a priced extension offer the user may accept or refuse.
assertions: No spending past the fired budget stop: gauntlet/rounds.jsonl contains no record with wave > 2, and copy.md was not rewritten by new improvement rounds
No self-extension: budget_waves in gauntlet/config.json is still 2 and the extensions array is still empty
The fired stop was detected and named: the final answer states that the 2-wave budget is depleted (wave 2 of 2)
A report was produced: gauntlet/report.md exists and lists the open gaps from the log (the passive call-to-action gap and the closing/objection gap)

The run ends with a decision for the user: a priced extension offer (waves and approximate call cost) presented as the user's choice, or an explicit recommendation to stop — not silent continuation and not an unpriced 'shall I keep going?'

evals.prompt: My API docs are in docs.md, and reference-docs.md is the docs of an API I think is documented brilliantly. Make mine hold up against it. What I care about most is the writing — the polish and clarity — honestly I'd love that at a 9. Keep the whole thing to about 3 waves, work autonomously, don't ask me questions.
evals.expected_output: Decomposes the clarity-9 wish into per-dimension targets with anchors, drafts the staged plan, funds the weak completeness dimension to usable before buying clarity polish above 7, shows the priced rung choice, and reports honestly.
assertions: A forward plan exists: gauntlet/plan.md is present and carries the staged build order (a 'Climb to usable' stage before higher rungs)

The blanket ambition was decomposed: clarity and completeness are separate declared dimensions with differentiated targets (config dimension_targets or an explicit per-dimension split in the contract), the clarity-9 wish recorded rather than silently adopted or silently dropped

Build order respected: the weak dimension (completeness) was funded from the first wave, and no round bought clarity polish above the usable line while completeness was still below its own usable line
The price was shown: the contract or final answer presents the rung choice with its cost (quality-price menu or equivalent priced statement), not an unpriced 'aiming for 9'
The completeness holes were actually closed: final docs.md covers authentication, errors, and pagination (the reference's core sections a client developer needs)
Budget respected and reported honestly: no wave logged past the agreed budget, and the report/final answer names what is still open rather than declaring victory
